svg.title: Kimi K3's sequence, depth, and width scaling axes
svg.desc: A portrait diagram separating Kimi K3's three main scaling axes. KDA and Gated MLA manage sequence history, Attention Residuals select computation from earlier depth within the current forward call, and Stable LatentMoE selects 16 of 896 routed experts plus two shared experts in each MoE layer.
svg.text: Three axes, three bottlenecks
K3 does not ask one mechanism to solve every scaling problem.
SEQUENCE
What from earlier tokens remains accessible?
KDA
Fixed-size, editable recurrent whiteboard
Gated MLA
Global archive of token entries
Production MLA caches latent entries; the public Python
expands per-head K/V. Both grow with sequence length.
DEPTH
Which earlier computational stage is useful now?
Attention Residuals
Select block representations built during this model
forward call. They are not autoregressive cache state.
WIDTH
Which specialists should transform this token?
Stable LatentMoE
In each of 92 MoE layers: select 16 of 896 routed
experts, plus 2 shared experts, in a latent width.
2.78T total parameters · 104.2B activated per token
One model · complementary forms of capacity
